final:
Using: film-crew (Villeneuve lens, full mode), then seedance-25-director for the final prompt.

**Setup notes:** This folder isn't a git repo and has no `NOTES.md`, so there were no open items to read and nothing to commit or push. I also found no saved facts about «Թարգմանչուհին», so I invented the characters' looks and the setting myself. Change them if they don't match the script.

**The scene:** 20 s, 4 shots, 16:9, made as one Seedance 2.5 call with three cuts inside it. One call keeps faces, the room and the light consistent across the cuts better than four separate clips would.

| # | s | Shot | Beat | Cut to next |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0–6 | Wide shot from behind two elders, 24mm, very slow push-in to medium wide | The manager says in English: "There is no blasting on this mountain. None." Narine stands at his side. | The rumble starts at 5 s, before the cut |
| 2 | 6–10 | Close-up of a water glass, 100mm macro, camera still | Rings form on the water and the glass creeps a few mm. The building says what he won't. | The rumble fades into the next shot |
| 3 | 10–15 | Medium close-up of Narine, 85mm, very slow push-in | His voice off-screen: "Just routine surveys. Please, translate." She doesn't speak. Her eyes drop to the floor, she swallows, then turns her head to the window. | Cut on her look |
| 4 | 15–20 | Wide shot over her right shoulder toward the window, 24mm | A pale column of dust rises behind the ridge. His reflection in the glass is still smiling at the elders. A distant boom arrives late, at 17 s. | Hold in silence |

**How the clips cut together:**
- **Room layout:** Narine always stands at the manager's left, on the window side. The window stays frame-right in shots 1–3.
- **Light:** one cold, overcast window light in every shot. No handheld camera, and no camera shake even during the tremor.
- **Cause before effect:** you hear the rumble before you see the ripples, and you see the dust before you hear the boom.

**Choices I made for you:**
- **Narine's silence:** Seedance 2.5 doesn't list Armenian as a dialogue language, so she has no line in the clip. Her failure to translate is the realisation. If you want her to start a sentence and stop, record it and add it in the edit.
- **Added in the edit:** the "Day 6" card, the music and the Armenian subtitles.

**Risks:**
- Without reference images, faces may drift a little between shots. Stills from banana-pro-director-2.0 would fix that; the four keyframe prompts are in `08_storyboard.md`.
- The reflection in the glass in shot 4 may not appear. The scene works without it.
- **Not checked yet:** there was no shell, so I checked the package against the validator's rules by hand. I couldn't run the independent continuity check either.

The full crew package (files 00–10) is in `film-crew/targmanchuhin-day6-tremor/`.

## FINAL

**Settings:** Dreamina → Seedance 2.5 → **Omni Reference** · Duration **20 s** · Ratio **16:9** · Resolution **720p** for tests, **1080p** for the final · no uploads · run 2–3 seeds.

```text
No reference files; text-only generation.

A restrained four-shot dramatic scene in a vast concrete boardroom of a mining company: a foreign manager calmly tells two local elders there is no blasting, the floor trembles under them, and his translator Narine falls silent as she realises the secret blasting has begun. Cold, slow, monumental, photoreal cinema.

Characters, identical in every shot:
Narine: an Armenian woman in her early thirties, slim, dark brown hair pulled back in a low tight bun with a few loose strands at the temple, dark tired eyes, no visible makeup, charcoal wool turtleneck sweater, dark grey straight trousers, thin silver wristwatch, white plastic visitor badge on a black lanyard, holding a small black notepad and a pen at waist height.
The manager: a European man in his late fifties, short silver hair, clean-shaven, composed face, navy blue suit, white shirt open at the collar with no tie, company badge clipped to the breast pocket.
The elders: two elderly local men seated with their backs to camera, dark wool coats, one in a flat cap, seen only as dark silhouettes.

Location, same in every shot: a vast top-floor boardroom of a mining company: raw board-formed grey concrete walls rising high, a long matte black table, black leather chairs, a polished grey concrete floor. The whole right wall is one floor-to-ceiling window looking out over a bare grey mountain ridge under a low white overcast sky, pale haze in the valley. On the table: a glass water carafe, clear glass tumblers of water, closed grey folders.
Light, same in every shot: soft cold overcast daylight from the tall window only, no ceiling lights, deep soft shadows, monochrome cold grey-blue palette, no warm light anywhere.

[0-6s] Shot 1. Wide shot, 24mm lens, camera at seated eye level behind the two elders' backs at the near end of the table, very slow dolly push-in along the table. The elders are dark silhouettes in the foreground. At the far head of the table the manager stands, small under the high concrete wall, the window on the right of frame; Narine stands one step to his left, nearer the window, pen ready. The manager rests his right hand beside a glass tumbler of water and says calmly in English: "There is no blasting on this mountain. None." The push ends on a medium wide shot of the manager and Narine. At 5 seconds a very deep low rumble begins under the room tone. No camera shake, nobody reacts yet.
[6-10s] Natural shot switch. Extreme close-up insert, 100mm macro lens, camera locked off at table height: the glass tumbler of water on the black table, the manager's navy cuff soft at the left edge of frame. The rumble swells; the flat water surface shivers into fine concentric rings and the tumbler creeps a few millimetres across the table, then the rings slowly fade as the rumble dies away. The glass does not fall, no water spills, the camera stays perfectly still.
[10-15s] Natural shot switch. Medium close-up of Narine, 85mm lens, eye level, three-quarter front, very shallow depth of field, very slow push-in, window light on the right side of her face. She faces left of frame toward the manager, lips just parted as if to translate. The manager's voice, off-screen, calm and smooth, in English: "Just routine surveys. Please, translate." Narine does not speak. Her breath stops, her eyes drop to the floor, her throat swallows once, then she slowly turns her head to the right until her eyes rest on the window, and she stays completely still. No words from Narine, no tears, no gasp, no large gesture.
[15-20s] Natural shot switch. Wide shot over Narine's right shoulder, 24mm lens, very slow push-in toward the window: the back of her head and low bun soft in the left foreground, the floor-to-ceiling window filling the frame as bright backlight, Narine a near-silhouette; the manager's faint reflection is visible in the glass, still smiling at the elders, not looking out. Far away behind the bare grey ridge, a slow pale column of dust rises silently into the overcast sky. At 17 seconds a distant muffled boom arrives, the window glass hums faintly and a thin line of dust sifts down from the top of the window frame. The shot holds on the rising dust in silence. No fire, no flash, no fireball, no debris near the building.

Global: one continuous scene in one room, the same cold overcast window light in every shot; the window is always on the right of frame in shots 1 to 3. The camera moves only by very slow push-ins or stays locked off; no handheld, no camera shake even during the tremor. Keep Narine, the manager and the elders identical in every shot; no extra people. Sound: quiet room tone, faint air-conditioning hum, the manager's two English lines only, a very deep low rumble from 5 to 10 seconds, near-silence, a distant muffled boom at 17 seconds, then silence. Pure video, no subtitles, no background music, no on-screen text, no logos, no warm colours.
```

**If one shot fails:** re-run only that shot in **First and Last Frames** mode. Use the frame just before the cut as the first frame and that shot's keyframe still from `08_storyboard.md` as the last frame. Same settings, at least 4 s.
